text.en: Asha sorted her class into the group of students who like cricket and the group who like football. "Some are in both groups," she noticed.

A set is a well-defined collection of objects. A set can be written in descriptive form, in set-builder form such as {x : x is a vowel} or in roster form such as {a, e, i, o, u}. Sets are named by capital letters and their members are called elements, which belong to the set.
There are many types of sets. The empty set has no element, a finite set has a countable number of elements and an infinite set does not end. Equal sets have the same elements, equivalent sets have the same number of elements, a subset is contained in another set and the power set of A is the set of all subsets of A, with 2^n elements if A has n elements.
Set operations are the union (all elements of A or B), intersection (elements common to both), difference and complement. De Morgan's laws say (A union B)' = A' intersect B' and (A intersect B)' = A' union B'. For two finite sets, n(A union B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A intersect B).
